correctness.rationale: Reconstructed L=2^d-W as the count of removed simplex-corner representatives, indexed by binary vertices. For two losses, deficit sum >= Hamming distance, while each deficit sum <a<1; hence Hamming distance=1. Three pairwise adjacent binary vertices cannot exist, so L<=2 for every d. Each of d 2^{d-1} cube edges has coincidence volume 2h^d/d! where h=(a-1/2)_+, so p2=2^d h^d/(d-1)!; E[L]=2^d a^d/d!, p1=E[L]-2p2 and p0=1-p1-p2. Integer Fourier coefficients of W equal those of the polytope and Parseval yields Var(L)=E[L]+2p2-E[L]^2. Differentiating the nonanalytic term 2^{d+1}h^d/(d-1)! produces jump 2^{d+1}d at order d. Positive-measure support arguments and h->1/2 supremum checked. Independently sampled 20,000 uniform torus points at (d,a)=(3,.2),(3,.75),(4,.75),(5,.95); all removals <=2 and frequencies near analytic masses. This Monte Carlo does not establish the universal theorem; the graph/simplex proof does.
